events.title: Sundar Pichai named Google CEO
events.summary: Google appointed Sundar Pichai CEO on August 10, 2015 as Alphabet reorganized — putting him in charge of search, Chrome, and Android.
events.about: Pichai steered Google through the mobile-to-AI transition — scaling Android, Chrome, and later Gemini. He represents the product-engineer path to leading the world's largest internet software stack.

narrative.whyChosen: Pichai leads the company whose platforms most developers build on or compete with.
narrative.whyImportant: His tenure spans mobile dominance and the generative AI race.
narrative.problemSolved: Google needed focused product leadership after the Alphabet split from experimental bets.

events.title: Phoenix 1.0 released
events.summary: Chris McCord released Phoenix 1.0 on August 28, 2015 — a productive Elixir web framework with channels for real-time WebSocket apps.
events.about: Phoenix brought Rails-like productivity to Elixir: generators, Ecto for databases, and channels for live updates. It powered Discord-scale chat, dashboards, and APIs where BEAM fault tolerance mattered — proving Elixir was more than a syntax experiment.

narrative.whyChosen: Phoenix 1.0 was the web framework that made Elixir production-credible.
narrative.whyImportant: Channels and OTP supervision brought real-time features without fragile Node clusters.
narrative.problemSolved: Elixir needed a batteries-included web stack to compete with Rails and Django.
